title: A partially linearized mapping approach to surface hopping (MASH-PLDM) for nonadiabatic dynamics and nonlinear spectroscopy
authors: Jan Obermeier, Kasra Asnaashari, Jeremy O. Richardson
abstract: We derive a partially linearized version of the mapping approach to surface hopping (MASH) that provides a new method for simulating nonadiabatic dynamics in molecular systems. As in the original MASH formalism, trajectories travel on adiabatic surfaces with hops determined by the dynamics of a spin vector on the Bloch sphere. However, because the new approach is based on the partially linearized density matrix (PLDM), it has two spin vectors, which may be in the same or different hemispheres of the Bloch sphere. The former scenario describes an electronic population moving on a single adiabatic surface, whereas the latter describes a coherence moving on the average surface. We show that this new method, called MASH-PLDM, leads to improved results over the original MASH dynamics for a variety of scattering problems and spin-boson models, especially in cases where coherences play an important role. A further benefit of the new methodology is that it can treat multi-time correlation functions such as those required for nonlinear spectroscopy. We demonstrate this capability with a proof-of-principle simulation of time-resolved pump-probe spectroscopy.
summary: The paper introduces MASH-PLDM, an advanced surface hopping technique that extends the standard MASH formalism by using a partially linearized density matrix. This allows the method to accurately treat electronic coherences, leading to improved results for nonadiabatic dynamics. Crucially, it provides a pathway to simulate complex multi-time correlation functions required for nonlinear spectroscopy.
main_problem: Developing a robust method to simulate nonadiabatic dynamics and calculate multi-time correlation functions in molecular systems.
main_result: The proposed MASH-PLDM method improves upon original MASH dynamics, particularly when electronic coherences are significant, and naturally extends to nonlinear spectroscopy measurements.
method: It employs a partially linearized mapping approach (PLDM) applied to the surface hopping formalism, utilizing two distinct spin vectors to track both population on single surfaces and coherence on an average surface.
model_or_system: The study focuses on nonadiabatic molecular dynamics, modeled using a two-level electronic system coupled to nuclear degrees of freedom, often analyzed via path integrals and spin vectors on the Bloch sphere.
key_observables: Time-dependent excited-state population, multi-time correlation functions (e.g., for time-resolved pump-probe spectroscopy).
important_parameters: The dynamics are governed by the electronic Hamiltonian and the coupling to nuclear motion, analyzed in the quasiclassical limit.
main_assumptions: The core approximation is the Partially Linearized Density Matrix (PLDM), which linearizes nuclear variables into an average path while treating electronic spin vectors separately.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the PLDM approximation to correlation functions and the time evolution of the spin vector, showing precession and rotation dynamics.
paper_structure: The paper develops the MASH-PLDM formalism by applying the PLDM approximation to the path integral representation of the correlation function, deriving new equations of motion for the nuclei, and validating the method against standard MASH approaches.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the simulation of open quantum systems and nonadiabatic processes crucial in molecular physics and quantum optics, providing an advanced, theoretically grounded trajectory-based method.

The PLDM approximation to the correlation function between ˆA at time 0 and ˆB at time t linearizes the nuclear variables of the forward and backward paths into the average path, ¯q. However, the spin vectors S and S′, which represent the electronic state, are not linearized and follow different forward and backward paths.

FIG. 2. Time evolution of the spin vector S induced by Eq. (8). It can be decomposed into two contributions: a rotation around the y-axis (out-of-plane) from the changing character of the adiabatic states; and a precession around the new z-axis on the dashed circle of latitude resulting from the energy difference between the adiabatic states, Vz.

FIG. 3. In MASH-PLDM, the nuclear force is determined based on the hemispheres in which the spins S and S′ are located. The force is that of the excited state if both spins are in the upper hemisphere, of the lower state if both are in the lower hemisphere, or averaged if they are in different hemispheres.
